query: Draft two review comments for acme/sdk#91, no need to post them. First: `sdk/cache.py` line 30 loads the whole cache file into memory on every lookup, which will hurt on large caches. I don't care how it's fixed, an LRU, an index, lazy loading, whatever, but I have one idea: memoize the parsed file with functools.lru_cache. Second: `sdk/auth.py` line 12 builds the token header by string concatenation; it has to use the existing `build_auth_header()` helper, because that's the only path that redacts the token in debug logs.
expected_behavior: Each comment opens with a plain-text conventional comment label
The cache comment leads with the problem (full file load per lookup) and why it matters, before any fix
The lru_cache idea is marked as one option or an example, and the comment makes clear any fix for the stated problem resolves it
The cache comment doesn't present lru_cache as a required implementation, either in prose or as a suggested-edit block without an illustrative marker
The auth comment prescribes build_auth_header() and states the reason in the same comment: it's the only path that redacts the token in debug logs
<!--:robot:--> is the literal last line of each comment
